newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rebounding Bunds post further gains vs Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Rebounding Bunds post further gains vs Treasuries.

text.p: Bund futures rebounded convincingly on Thursday from Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks, pushing the spread against Treasuries further into record high territory.
The DTB March Bund futures contract was up 27 basis points late in the day at 103.30, off an earlier high off 103.36.
But the real story of the day came on the spreads, where Bunds continued to outperform their U.S. counterparts, pushing the spread to 109 basis points from 101 basis points on Wednesday.
Although the spread may face technical trendline resistance near current levels, some analysts figure it could widen to near 120 basis points in coming weeks.
The case for a wider spread received fresh support today when the respected Ifo economic research institute fueled speculation of slow economic growth.
It said it expected an unemployment rate of 10.9 percent this year and that it would be nearly impossible for the government to achieve its stated goal of halving unemployment by the year 2000.
The benchmark 10-year Bund was 24 basis points higher in price at 103.26 to yield 5.56 percent.

Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer's speech this morning was the major event of the day, but his remarks mostly about European monetary union and currency markets failed to cast any light on his feelings about German monetary policy.

Some analysts expect the German yield curve to flatten somewhat with short term investors still hoping for lower German interest rates while the long-end of the curve will remain hostage to international markets.
Late in the the day, the yield curve spread between two- and 10-year maturities had narrowed by three basis points to 206 basis points.
Traders said they were encouraged that Bunds have twice climbed back above the 103.00 level after falling below that psychologically important point.
But a range between 103.00 and 103.50 or so is seen at least through early next week with no major events scheduled that would give traders reason to push the contract substantially.
